Decision: Selected customer segmentation as the primary lens
Options_Considered: Customer segmentation; product association; customer value and retention
Reason: The transaction data supports customer-level behavioural profiling through engineered purchasing features
Evidence: The dataset contains CustomerID, InvoiceDate, Quantity, and UnitPrice variables
Impact: Defines the main unit of analysis and modeling strategy

Decision: Selected product association and bundling as the secondary lens
Options_Considered: No secondary lens; overall association mining; segment-specific association mining
Reason: This directly strengthens the primary lens by producing product recommendations for suitable customer segments
Evidence: InvoiceNo and StockCode support basket construction while CustomerID connects baskets to customer segments
Impact: Adds coherent cross-selling and bundling recommendations

Decision: Excluded the raw Excel dataset from Git tracking
Options_Considered: Commit raw data to GitHub; store externally and document access
Selected_Option: Store externally and document the source, path, and fingerprint
Reason: The dataset is publicly available and approximately 23 MB; excluding it keeps the repository lightweight while preserving reproducibility
Evidence: The UCI dataset page, DOI, local path, and SHA-256 fingerprint are documented
Impact: Every member must download and verify the same dataset file

Options_Considered: Use unspecified seeds; use different seeds; use one documented seed
Reason: A fixed seed makes model fitting, sampling, and initial validation results reproducible
Evidence: The same seed can be reused across notebooks and verified by all members
Impact: Improves repeatability while stability will still be assessed using additional seeds

Decision: Investigated exact duplicate rows before preprocessing
Options_Considered: Retain all rows; remove every repeated InvoiceNo; retain one copy of exact duplicate records
Selected_Option: Retain one copy of each exact duplicate record
Reason: Repeated InvoiceNo values are legitimate because invoices contain multiple product lines, but exact repetition across all eight fields may inflate analytical measures
Evidence: 5268 additional exact duplicate rows were identified across 4879 duplicate groups
Impact: Exact duplicates will be removed during preprocessing while the raw dataset remains unchanged

Options_Considered: Include all transactions; exclude only C-prefixed invoices; require non-cancellation invoices with positive Quantity and UnitPrice
Selected_Option: Require non-cancellation InvoiceNo, Quantity greater than zero, and UnitPrice greater than zero
Reason: Cancellations, returns, stock adjustments, and non-positive prices can distort purchase revenue and RFM measures
Evidence: 9288 cancellation rows, 10624 negative-quantity rows, and 2517 non-positive-price rows were identified
Impact: Creates a valid purchase-only source while retaining excluded records separately for investigation

Decision: Defined CustomerID handling by analytical task
Options_Considered: Impute missing IDs; treat each missing row as a customer; exclude missing IDs from customer-level analysis
Selected_Option: Exclude missing CustomerID rows from customer segmentation and segment-specific rules
Reason: Missing customer identifiers cannot be reliably reconstructed or assigned to a customer
Evidence: 135080 rows have missing CustomerID, representing 24.93 percent of the raw data
Impact: Customer segmentation coverage is reduced, but invalid customer attribution and fabricated identities are avoided

Decision: Selected StockCode as the product identifier
Options_Considered: Use Description; use StockCode; combine StockCode and Description as separate products
Selected_Option: Use StockCode with a canonical description for reporting
Reason: StockCode is the stable item identifier while descriptions contain spelling and naming variations
Impact: Prevents the same product from being split into several items during association mining

Decision: Defined preliminary handling of administrative StockCodes
Options_Considered: Treat all codes as merchandise; remove every code without digits; use an explicit reviewed administrative-code list
Selected_Option: Use an explicit reviewed administrative-code list
Reason: Some letter-only codes are genuine merchandise while other codes represent fees, postage, samples, or adjustments
Evidence: 2310 candidate administrative rows worth GBP 394205.67 were identified; DCGSSBOY and DCGSSGIRL are genuine products
Impact: Administrative codes will be excluded from product association rules and tested through monetary-feature sensitivity analysis

Options_Considered: Remove all IQR outliers; cap automatically; investigate and compare transformations
Selected_Option: Retain extreme observations for investigation and perform transformation and sensitivity analysis
Reason: Large observations may represent genuine wholesale customers rather than errors
Evidence: Maximum valid line quantity is 80995 and maximum valid line value is GBP 168469.60; top 1 percent of customers generate 32.20 percent of revenue
Impact: Prevents unjustified information loss while requiring log transformation, robust scaling, and stability checks

Decision: Flagged the final month as incomplete
Options_Considered: Treat every month equally; remove December 2011; retain and explicitly flag the partial month
Selected_Option: Retain December 2011 and flag it as partial
Reason: The dataset ends on 09 December 2011, so the final month cannot be compared directly with complete monthly totals
Evidence: December 2011 contains records only from 01 to 09 December
Impact: Recency calculations can use the latest date, but seasonality conclusions must identify the incomplete month

Decision: Recognised geographic imbalance in the analysis
Options_Considered: Restrict immediately to UK; encode Country in clustering; retain all countries and conduct sensitivity analysis
Selected_Option: Retain all countries initially and consider a UK-only sensitivity analysis
Reason: The full dataset provides broader coverage, but the dominant UK market could control cluster patterns
Evidence: The UK represents 91.45 percent of valid purchase rows and 84.59 percent of valid purchase revenue
Impact: Country will not automatically be used as a distance feature; geographic limitations and sensitivity results will be reported

Options_Considered: Create one universal cleaned dataset; create separate datasets for segmentation association rules returns and administrative records
Reason: Customer segmentation and association mining require different units of analysis and eligibility conditions
Evidence: Final outputs contain 391150 customer-merchandise rows 522568 basket rows 10587 return-adjustment rows and 2310 administrative rows
Impact: Prevents one cleaning rule from incorrectly removing information required by another task

Options_Considered: Retain imported types; convert identifiers to numeric measures; standardise identifiers as categorical values
Selected_Option: Standardise text fields and convert identified CustomerID values to integer identifiers
Reason: InvoiceNo StockCode and CustomerID are identifiers rather than continuous measurements; consistent formatting prevents grouping errors
Evidence: Standardisation created zero additional duplicate records and valid purchase descriptions contained zero missing values
Impact: Produces consistent invoice product and customer grouping keys for downstream analysis

Options_Considered: Use raw Quantity multiplied by UnitPrice; calculate after filtering; omit transaction value
Selected_Option: Calculate LineTotal as positive Quantity multiplied by positive UnitPrice after purchase-validity filtering
Reason: Calculating after validation prevents cancellations returns and invalid prices from being treated as positive purchase revenue
Evidence: All 391150 primary customer merchandise rows have positive Quantity UnitPrice and LineTotal
Impact: Provides a valid monetary measure for RFM and customer-value features

Decision: Excluded generated processed datasets from Git and recorded fingerprints
Options_Considered: Commit large processed CSV files; exclude them without evidence; regenerate locally and record fingerprints
Selected_Option: Regenerate processed datasets locally and document row counts file sizes and SHA-256 fingerprints
Reason: Processed datasets are reproducible from the verified raw file and executable preprocessing notebook while Git remains lightweight
Evidence: All four processed files passed reload validation and their SHA-256 fingerprints were saved
Impact: Each member can reproduce and verify identical processed outputs before downstream analysis
